newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel best placed for Thomson - chair.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel best placed for Thomson - chair.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom will use its acquisition of Thomson, if its bid for the company is successful, to build one of the world's top electronics groups and needs no financial support for its bid, Alcatel's chairman Serge Tchuruk said on Tuesday in a newspaper interview.
In the interview in daily Le Figaro, Tchuruk said Alcatel was looking for an Asian partner for Thomson Multimedia to give it a better position in Asian markets.
Tchuruk said Thomson and Alcatel were extremely complementary companies and that both would benefit from an Alcatel takeover.
Alcatel is bidding against Lagardere Group for the right to take over state-owned Thomson SA. The government's decision on the winning bid is expected around mid-month.
"I can say that we need no financial support from any partner at all...this leaves our hands free for the future," Tchuruk said.

"When we assess the complementarity between the two companies, there are 33 billion francs of turnover of Thomson-CSF (or more than 90 percent of the total) which can be joined with 74 billion francs of Alcatel turnover," he said.

"The result would represent more than 100 billion francs of civil and military electronics business and would place the company among the very largest of the world's electronics firms," Tchuruk added.

Thanks to its large size in civil electronic systems and its presence in most of the sector's businesses, Alcatel Alsthom is by far the best placed to assure the development of Thomson's non-military businesses, Tchuruk said.
But he said this strength in consumer electronics should not hide his objective of making Thomson-CSF the world's second largest defence electronics company.
Tchuruk said he hoped to hold on to a stake in SGS-Thomson and hoped to see cooperation between it and the new strengthened company.
"I think it would be too bad if Thomson-CSF's stake in the capital of SGS-Thomson was sold without analysing ways of reinforcing that cooperation," he said.
